thread:
Carla (Support): FYI we got an angry escalation from AcmePayments — they saw a sudden wave of 429s around 14:05 UTC. They say calls were steady then a batch job kicked off and clients hit 429s for ~3m. Ticket #SUP-13287.

Dave (AcmePayments): they sent these logs: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-...' \
  -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\n> x-ratelimit-retry-after: 3\n```
They reported `x-ratelimit-bucket: customer:acme` header too.

Alice (eng-sre): thanks, copying in eng-runtime. Do we have sampling for that customer around 14:00? Any config changes rolled recently?

Bob (eng-runtime): looking now. No deploys in the last 12h for limiter code. I see a spike on the token-bucket refill queue for customer:acme at 14:04:02 — concurrent bursts hit the per-customer burst allowance (burst_tokens=20) and then enforcement switched to strict mode.

Bob (eng-runtime): paste of logs (trimmed):
```
2026-11-06T14:04:02Z limiter DEBUG bucket=customer:acme tokens_left=0 refill_rate=0.5 rps=90
2026-11-06T14:04:03Z limiter WARN enforce_strict=true dropped=45
```
Looks like a scheduled Acme batch job sent ~90 rps for ~20s. Our smoothing window is 10s which caused tokens to deplete.

Carla (Support): Acme said they didn't change anything on their side — it's a nightly reconciliation job that usually runs at 02:00 UTC, but their ops team moved it to 14:00 for testing.

Eve (Customer Success): pinging Acme contact for confirmation and to ask for a reduced retry policy while we triage.

Alice (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) emergency bump per-customer burst_tokens to 200 for acme; 2) temporarily relax `enforce_strict` to false for that bucket; 3) apply a global smoothing throttle to allow short spikes through. Option 1 is safest for this single customer. Thoughts?

Bob (eng-runtime): Option 1 is doable via feature flag and doesn't require code deploy. I can flip a flag for `bucket_override.acme=burst:200` but it will increase risk of downstream GPU queue pressure if they truly blast sustained traffic. We should timebox the override to ~30m.

Carla (Support): Acme is asking for a short window to finish the tests (they estimated 12m). Can we do the override for 20m and keep monitoring?

Alice (eng-sre): agree. Also add an alert to catch sustained queue length > 60s for any pool we route them to.

DeployBot: Applying config change: `bucket_override.acme=burst:200; expiry=2026-11-06T14:30:00Z` — rollout to limiter-config v2 -> 3 nodes at 14:08:12Z.

Bob (eng-runtime): change applied. Observability shows immediate drop in 429s for that bucket. Metrics snippet: 14:05-14:25 
- pre-change 429 count (acme): 128
- post-change 429 count (acme): 3
- gpu-queue-latency median: 85ms -> 92ms (no meaningful increase)

Dave (AcmePayments): confirmed 429s stopped after your change. Thanks. We'll keep our test client at 40rps while you monitor.

Carla (Support): marking ticket SUP-13287 as "mitigated" pending post-incident follow-up.

Alice (eng-sre): Post-incident action items (rough):
- short-term: create a per-customer burst override playbook (who can flip, TTL defaults, monitoring).
- medium-term: implement adaptive smoothing so small spikes < 30s get smoothed without burning burst tokens.
- long-term: expose per-customer burst quota to console with alerting and allow customers to request temporary increases.
- metrics: add histo for `burst_consumption_seconds` and a per-bucket retry-rate signal.

Bob (eng-runtime): also found a small bug in the limiter code where `refill_rate` was computed using the wrong window when `enforce_strict` toggles quickly — can cause transient over-enforcement. I'll open an MR to fix and add unit tests.

Alice (eng-sre): great. Please include in the postmortem the exact sequence: backlog spike -> burst tokens exhausted -> strict mode enforcement -> 429s. That will help justify the adaptive smoothing work.

Eve (Customer Success): I'll coordinate a short write-up to Acme explaining the root cause and our actions and include a recommendation to not reschedule production batch jobs into peak windows without coordination.

Bob (eng-runtime): MR opened: #RWD-4891 "fix refill window bug". Targeting merge in next patch release.

Alice (eng-sre): I've created the postmortem doc draft: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pm-13287 (please add notes). Assigning owners: Bob -> runtime fix, Alice -> alerts/monitoring, Eve -> external comms, Carla -> playbook creation.

Carla (Support): closing loop with Acme: they requested an explicit TTL and visibility. I'll add that to playbook.

Dave (AcmePayments): appreciated — we'll also add a flag on our side to gate the job if we detect >50rps sustained.

Alice (eng-sre): OK team, leave this thread if no further blocker. We'll follow up in the postmortem and schedule a 30-min retro tomorrow 10:00 PST to finalize mitigations. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: Reminder — config override `bucket_override.acme` expired at 2026-11-06T14:30:01Z and was garbage-collected.
